verses.zh: 摩西将以色列众人召了来，对他们说：「以色列人哪，我今日晓谕你们的律例典章，你们要听，可以学习，谨守遵行。
verses.en: Then Moses called all the people of Israel together and said to them:[NOTE:1] “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and ordinances that I am about to deliver to you today; learn them and be careful to keep them!
notes: Heb “and Moses called to all Israel and he said to them”; NAB, NASB, NIV “Moses summoned (convened NRSV) all Israel.”
verses.commentary:
5:1 "all Israel" The Law was for every Israelite (not an elite group), but Moses probably spoke to the elders who
then told his words to all the people (i.e. families, tribes, clans).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

▣ "Hear" See note at Deut. 4:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "the statutes and the ordinances" See note at Deut. 4:1 and
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

▣ "learn them and observe them carefully" This phrase has three VERBALS:

- "learn them" (BDB 540, KB 531, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:10; 5:1; 14:23; 17:19; 18:9; 31:12,13

- "observe them" (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:2,6,9,40; 5:10,12,29,32;
6:2,3, 17 [twice], 25; 7:8,9[twice],11,12[twice], etc.

- "carefully," literally "do" (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)

These three VERBALS summarize the meaning of shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570,
e.g. Deut. 4:1; 5:1,23,24,25,26, 27 [twice], 28 [twice]; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:9), which means "hear so as to do"! Spiritual
knowledge and a godly obedient lifestyle are both crucial!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神在何烈山与我们立约。
verses.en: The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
verses.commentary:
5:2 "The Lord our God" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

▣ "made" This is literally "cut" (BDB 503, KB 500, Qal PERFECT [twice]). This was a
method of OT covenant ratification (i.e. "to cut a covenant," cf. Gen. 15:18; 21:27,32; 31:44; Exod. 34:27; Deut. 5:3; 29:12; 31:16).
Abraham took a goat, a bull, and other animals, cut them in half, laid the halves on each side, and walked through the middle
of those halves as a sign of covenant. It possibly implies a curse on those who break the covenant (cf. Gen. 15:9-18; Jer. 34:18)
or even a meal to seal the covenant.

▣ "covenant with us" See note at Deut. 4:13.

▣ "at Horeb" Horeb is the Hebrew word for Mt. Sinai.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

verses.zh: 这约不是与我们列祖立的，乃是与我们今日在这里存活之人立的。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] did not make this covenant with our ancestors[NOTE:2] but with us, we who are here today, all of us living now.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “fathers.”
verses.commentary:
5:3 "our fathers" Some scholars see this phrase referring to the Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but
others see it referring to the parents, the evil generation who died in the wilderness (cf. Num. 26:63-65). The next
phrase seems to confirm the second option.

▣ "with all those of us alive here today" This refers to the children (i.e. under twenty years) of the
evil generation. This clearly shows that the words of YHWH had relevance to this generation and every generation, including today.

verses.zh: 耶和华在山上，从火中，面对面与你们说话―
verses.en: The Lord spoke face to face with you at the mountain, from the middle of the fire.
verses.commentary:
5:4 "face to face" This refers to a personal encounter (not literally) at Mt. Horeb/Sinai in Exodus 19-20. It is a recurrent
idiom (cf. Gen. 32:30; Exod. 33:11; Deut. 5:4; 34:10; Jdgs. 6:22; Ezek. 20:35).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FACE TO FACE

▣ "from the midst of the fire" This is a repeated reference to Exodus 19-20 (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33,36; 5:4,22,24,26; 9:10; 10:4).

verses.zh: 那时我站在耶和华和你们中间，要将耶和华的话传给你们；因为你们惧怕那火，没有上山―说：
verses.en: (I was standing between the Lord and you at that time to reveal the Lord’s message to you, because you were afraid of the fire and would not go up the mountain.) He said:
verses.commentary:
5:5 "while I was standing between the Lord and you. . .for you were afraid" The people
were afraid of YHWH so Moses acted as a mediator between YHWH and the Israelites (cf. Exod. 19:16).

verses.zh: 「『我是耶和华―你的　神，曾将你从埃及地为奴之家领出来。
verses.en: “I am the Lord your God—he who brought you from the land of Egypt, from the place of slavery.
verses.commentary:
5:6 "I am the Lord" This may be paraphrased: "I am the 'I Am.'" I am the ever living,
only living God. I am the ever existing One. YHWH is a form of the Hebrew VERB "to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "who brought you out of the land of Egypt" Notice that YHWH's grace and elective choice came before
the Law was given. God chose Israel, she did not choose him. This choice was made plain to Abraham in the
unconditional promise/covenant of Gen. 15:12-21. YHWH's redemptive plan is unconditional but how it impacts
individuals and nations is conditional.

verses.zh: 「『除了我以外，你不可有别的神。
verses.en: “You must not have any other gods[NOTE:1] besides me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “there must not be for you other gods.” The expression “for you” indicates possession.

Heb “upon my face,” or “before me” (עַל־פָּנָיַ, ʿal panaya). Some understand this in a locative sense: “in my sight.” The translation assumes that the phrase indicates exclusion. The idea is that of placing any other god before the Lord in the sense of taking his place. Contrary to the view of some, this does not leave the door open for a henotheistic system where the Lord is the primary god among others. In its literary context the statement must be taken in a monotheistic sense. See, e.g., 4:39; 6:13-15.
verses.commentary:
5:7 "no other gods before Me" "Before" (BDB 818 #7) is literally "before My Face," which is an idiom
for "no other in My category" (cf. Exod. 20:3,23). YHWH is alone, unique, ever-existing! This is an assertion of monotheism
(cf. Exod. 8:10; 9:14; Deut. 4:35,39; 33:26; 1 Sam. 2:2; 2 Sam. 7:22; 22:32; Isa. 46:9). This first assertion and command is the
uniqueness of Israel's faith in a polytheistic Ancient Near East! See note at Deut. 6:4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

verses.zh: 「『不可为自己雕刻偶像，也不可做甚么形像，彷佛上天、下地和地底下、水中的百物。
verses.en: “You must not make for yourself an image[NOTE:1] of anything in heaven above, on earth below, or in the waters beneath.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “an image, any likeness.”
Heb “under the earth” (so ASV, NASB, NRSV); NCV “below the land.”
verses.commentary:
5:8 "an idol" This is literally "graven image" (BDB 820). This can refer to

- any physical representation of YHWH (cf. Deut. 4:12,15-19,23,25). The golden calf of Exodus 32 was a representation of YHWH

- foreign idols (cf. Lev. 19:4; 26:1)

▣ "earth" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY,
EARTH (ארץ)

verses.zh: 不可跪拜那些像，也不可事奉它，因为我耶和华―你的　神是忌邪的　神。恨我的，我必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三、四代；
verses.en: You must not worship or serve them, for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God. I punish[NOTE:1] the sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons for the sin of the fathers who reject[NOTE:2] me,[NOTE:3]
notes: In the Hebrew text the form is a participle, which is subordinated to what precedes. For the sake of English style, the translation divides this lengthy verse into two sentences.

Heb “who hate” (so NAB, NIV, NLT). Just as “to love” (אָהֵב, ʾahev) means in a covenant context “to choose, obey,” so “to hate” (שָׂנֵא, saneʾ) means “to reject, disobey” (cf. the note on the word “loved” in Deut 4:37; see also 5:10).

Heb “visiting the sin of fathers upon sons and upon a third (generation) and upon a fourth (generation) of those who hate me.” God sometimes punishes children for the sins of a father (cf. Num 16:27, 32; Josh 7:24-25; 2 Sam 21:1-9). On the principle of corporate solidarity and responsibility in OT thought see J. Kaminsky, Corporate Responsibility in the Hebrew Bible (JSOTSup). In the idiom of the text, the father is the first generation and the “sons” the second generation, making grandsons the third and great-grandsons the fourth. The reference to a third and fourth generation is a way of emphasizing that the sinner’s punishment would last throughout his lifetime. In this culture, where men married and fathered children at a relatively young age, it would not be unusual for one to see his great-grandsons. In an Aramaic tomb inscription from Nerab dating to the seventh century b.c., Agbar observes that he was surrounded by “children of the fourth generation” as he lay on his death bed (see ANET 661). The language of the text differs from Exod 34:7, the sons are the first generation, the grandsons (literally, “sons of the sons”) the second, great-grandsons the third, and great-great-grandsons the fourth. One could argue that formulation in Deut 5:9 (see also Exod 20:5) is elliptical/abbreviated or that the text suffers from an accidental scribal omission (the repetition of the words “sons” would invite accidental omission).
verses.commentary:
5:9 "You shall not worship them or serve them" These are two negated VERB forms:

- "worship" ‒ BDB 1005, KB 295 Hishtaphel IMPERFECT or Hithpael
IMPERFECT, which means "bow down," "prostrate" (cf. Deut. 4:19; 8:19; 11:16; Exod. 20:5; 23:24; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

- "serve" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, Hophal IMPERFECT, which means "do" "serve as
a slave," or "perform acts of worship (cf. Deut. 13:2; Exod. 20:5; 23:24

YHWH knew the "religious" and "superstitious" tendency of the fallen human heart and tried to
protect the revelation of Himself and His purposes from the destructive influences of Near Eastern idolatry.
Superstition is a terrible thing!

▣ "jealous" See note at Deut. 4:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUS. . .ZEALOUS

▣ The VERB "visiting" (BDB 823, KB 955, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)
has several senses:

- visit to bless ‒ Gen. 21:1; 50:24,25; Exod. 13:19; Ruth 1:6; Ps. 65:9; 106:4; Jer. 27:22; 29:10; 32:5

- visit to punish ‒ Exod. 20:5; 34:7; Jer. 11:22; 13:21; 21:14; 24:25; Amos 3:2,14; Hosea 1:4; 2:15; 4:14; 12:2

Context, context, context; clarifies lexical options!

▣ "the iniquity of the fathers" The term "iniquity" (BDB 730) may be related to the similar root,
"to twist" (BDB 730, e.g. 2 Sam. 19:20; 24:17; 1 Kgs. 8:47; Ps. 106:6). Israel is punished for her disobedience (e.g. Exod. 20:5;
34:7; Lev. 18:25; Num. 14:18; Deut. 19:15; Jer. 25:12; 36:31; Amos 3:2).

- iniquity ‒ עון

- twist ‒ עוה

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN IN THE OT, A. 2.

▣ "on the children, and on the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me" Notice the
punishment is not arbitrary or indiscriminate, but directed toward those who "hate" YHWH (BDB 971, KB 1338,
Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE). This implies that unbelief runs through families. The influence
of the parents is crucial to the development of faith (see notes at Deut. 4:10). In the ANE several generations of
families lived together. One generation's unbelief and/or disobedience affected the entire family. This is part of
the Hebrew concept of corporality (i.e. one affects the whole—Adam, Achan, David, Jesus).

To this sense of corporality must be added the individual aspect of faith (cf. Deut. 24:16;
2 Kgs. 14:6; Jer. 31:29-30; Ezekiel 18)!

Just a personal note, all of us come from sinful families. All of us are affected by them. The
sins of the parents are passed on to the children. But, thank God for

- Deut. 7:9, where the faith of the godly parents (not sinless) is passed on, not to the third and fourth generations
but to the thousandth generations (note Deut. 5:10).

- Ezekiel 18. The sin of a parent does not necessarily affect the faith of the children.

Sin has consequences through time, but faith also has consequences through time and eternity.

verses.zh: 爱我、守我诫命的，我必向他们发慈爱，直到千代。
verses.en: but I show covenant faithfulness[NOTE:1] to the thousands[NOTE:2] who choose[NOTE:3] me and keep my commandments.
notes: This theologically rich term (חֶסֶד, khesed) describes God’s loyalty to those who keep covenant with him. Sometimes it is used synonymously with בְּרִית (berit, “covenant”; Deut 7:9), and sometimes interchangeably with it (Deut 7:12). See H.-J. Zobel, TDOT 5:44-64.

Another option is to understand this as referring to “thousands (of generations) of those who love me” (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). See Deut 7:9. tc By a slight emendation (לֲאַלֻּפִים [laʾallufim] for לַאֲלָפִים [laʾalafim]) “clans” could be read in place of the MT reading “thousands.” However, no ms or versional evidence exists to support this emendation.
Heb “love.” See note on the word “reject” in v. 9.
verses.commentary:
5:10 "showing" This VERB (BDB 793, KB 889) is a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE,
which matches the ongoing action of the VERB in Deut. 5:9.

▣ "lovingkindness" This refers to YHWH's covenant love and loyalty.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "to thousands" These two verses help me see the nature of YHWH. His basic nature is
longsuffering love, but He does punish those who wilfully reject Him (especially those who have some knowledge
of His revelation, i.e. the covenant people). The numbers in these two verses make my point.

- visiting iniquity to the third and fourth generations

- showing covenant love to the thousandth generation (cf. Deut. 7:9)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

▣ "those who love Me and keep My commandments" It is a characteristic of Deuteronomy to link
obedience to YHWH's covenant to love for YHWH (cf. Deut. 6:5; 7:9; 10:12; 11:1,13,22; 13:3; 19:9; 30:6,16,20).

YHWH's love is not capricious, but clearly defined. He shows no partiality. His initiating covenant
love (i.e. unconditional promise of mankind's redemption) is maintained by covenant obedience (i.e. conditional covenant
of YHWH's mandated human response).

"Keep" (BDB 1036, KB 1581) is the key concept in this chapter (cf. Deut. 5:1,10,12,29,32 and
many more times in Deuteronomy). The OT was based on the grace of YHWH and lifetime human obedience/performance. YHWH
wanted to show human's inability to respond appropriately (cf. Galatians 3). The NT (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36) is
based on God's gracious initiation and redemption in Christ. Believers are still destined to be righteous (cf. Eph. 1:14; 2:10),
but they have been accepted and forgiven by grace through faith (cf. Eph. 2:8-9). Now they obey/perform out of a sense
of gratitude and family love (i.e. "those who love Me"). The goal is the same, a righteous (Christlike) people, but the
mechanism has changed from human performance to Christ's performance (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 「『不可妄称耶和华―你　神的名；因为妄称耶和华名的，耶和华必不以他为无罪。
verses.en: “You must not make use of the name of the Lord your God for worthless purposes,[NOTE:1] for the Lord will not exonerate anyone who abuses his name that way.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “take up the name of the Lord your God to emptiness”; KJV “take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.” The idea here is not cursing or profanity in the modern sense of these terms, but rather the use of the divine Name for unholy, mundane purposes, that is, for meaningless (Hebrew שָׁוְא [shavʾ]) and empty ends. In ancient Israel this would include using the Lord’s name as a witness in vows one did not intend to keep.
Heb “who takes up his name to emptiness.”
verses.commentary:
5:11 "You shall not take the name. . ." The VERB (BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT) means
"to lift," to carry," or "to take." It seems to imply an act of speech. The Israelites were called on to speak "the name" in
worship (cf. Deut. 6:13; 10:20), but not the name of other gods!

This emphasis begins in Gen. 4:25-26, where the line of Seth "began to call upon the name of
the Lord"; Abraham did the same (Gen. 12:8; 21:33); Isaac did the same (Gen. 26:25). This
same concept is put in an eschatological setting by Joel 2:28-32. This is continued by the Apostle Peter on Pentecost
and asserted to be fulfilled (cf. Acts 2:14-21); the Apostle Paul uses the phrase to offer universal salvation in Rom. 10:9-13.

The name represents the person and character of YHWH. The Israelites were to be a kingdom
of priests to the world (cf. Exod. 19:5-6), but the tragedy is that their covenant disobedience, which caused YHWH
to punish them (cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29), meant that the message to the world was distorted by:

- God's judgment of Israel instead of blessing

- God's people turning to idolatry

- God's people's developing arrogance, exclusiveness, and self-righteousness!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF THE LORD

▣ "in vain" This term (BDB 996) means "empty," "non-existent," "vain" (cf. Exod. 20:7; Ps. 139:20). This
is the same word used in Deut. 5:20 for a "false" witness. It is possible that this commandment does not refer to taking
oaths in YHWH's name (cf. Deut. 6:13; 10:20), but in using His name in false legal testimony. Israel became a "false" witness
to the character and purposes of YHWH because of their recurrent disobedience, which resulted in YHWH's judgment
(cf. Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

▣ "for the Lord will not leave him unpunished" The VERB
(BDB 667, KB 720, Piel IMPERFECT which means "acquit") is imagery for something clean,
thereby innocent or free from guilt (cf. Exod. 20:7; 34:7; Num. 14:18; Jer. 30:11; 46:28; Joel 3:21; Nah. 1:3). There are
consequences to human sin. To misrepresent YHWH is a most serious sin, especially for those who know Him
(cf. Luke 12:48; Heb. 10:26-31)!

verses.zh: 「『当照耶和华―你　神所吩咐的守安息日为圣日。
verses.en: “Be careful to observe[NOTE:1] the Sabbath day just as the Lord your God has commanded you.
notes: Heb “to make holy,” that is, to put to special use, in this case, to sacred purposes (cf. vv. 13-15).
verses.commentary:
5:12 "Observe" This VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE)
means "keep" and is used repeatedly in Deuteronomy.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "the sabbath" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT)

▣ "holy" This term (BDB 992) means "rest" or "cessation of activity." The usage as a day of worship starts with
Gen. 2:2-3, where YHWH uses His rest as a pattern for animals (cf. Exod. 23:12) and mankind (humans need a regular
schedule of work, rest, and worship). The first specialized use of this day by Israel was in Exod. 16:25-26 in the gathering
of manna. It then becomes part of "the Ten Words" (cf. Exod. 20:8-11; Deut. 5:12-15). This is one example where the Ten
Words in Exodus 20 are slightly different from the Ten Words in Deuteronomy 5. Deuteronomy is preparing Israel for the
settled, agricultural life in Canaan, while Exodus 20 dealt with their desert wandering period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

verses.zh: 六日要劳碌做你一切的工，
verses.en: You are to work and do all your tasks in six days,
verses.commentary:
5:13 "work" Laws like Deut. 5:13-14 caused the development of the Oral Traditions (i.e. Mishnah, Talmud, cf. Matt. 5:21-48) to be
written because a question like, "What is work?" became crucial. The rabbis devised a definition so that the faithful
Jew would not break the Law. The ambiguity of the written Law caused the legalistic Oral Law to be developed.

verses.zh: 但第七日是向耶和华―你　神当守的安息日。这一日，你和你的儿女、仆婢、牛、驴、牲畜，并在你城里寄居的客旅，无论何工都不可做，使你的仆婢可以和你一样安息。
verses.en: but the seventh day is the Sabbath[NOTE:1] of the Lord your God. On that day you must not do any work, you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any other animal, or the resident foreigner who lives with you,[NOTE:2] so that your male and female slaves, like yourself, may have rest.
notes: There is some degree of paronomasia (wordplay) here: “the seventh (הַשְּׁבִיעִי, hasheviʿi) day is the Sabbath (שַׁבָּת, shabbat).” Otherwise, the words have nothing in common, since “Sabbath” is derived from the verb שָׁבַת (shavat, “to cease”).
Heb “in your gates”; NRSV, CEV “in your towns”; TEV “in your country.”
verses.commentary:
5:14 "seventh day is a sabbath" The Sabbath was a day of rest (BDB 992). There are two origins given for the Sabbath:
Exodus 20:11 orients it to Genesis 1-2, while Deuteronomy orients it to the Egyptian bondage (cf. Deut. 5:15). It became a
covenant marker (like circumcision) of YHWH's people (cf. Exod. 31:13,17; Ezek. 20:12,20). Obedience was mandated
(cf. Isa. 56:2; 58:13; Jer. 17:21-22).

Like the sun, moon (cf. Gen. 1:14), and seasons, the Sabbath provided a division of time for mankind's activities
(cf. Ecclesiastes 3). The seven day week became a way to mark special days and years (cf. Exodus 23 and Leviticus 23).
Specifically, the Sabbath begins on Friday evening and goes through Saturday evening, because Israelites marked the
day in Genesis 1 categories ("evening and morning," cf. Gen. 1:5,8,13,19,23,31).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT)

verses.zh: 你也要记念你在埃及地作过奴仆；耶和华―你　神用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂将你从那里领出来。因此，耶和华―你的　神吩咐你守安息日。
verses.en: Recall that you were slaves in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God brought you out of there by strength and power.[NOTE:1] That is why the Lord your God has commanded you to observe[NOTE:2] the Sabbath day.
notes: Heb “by a strong hand and an outstretched arm,” the hand and arm symbolizing divine activity and strength. Cf. NLT “with amazing power and mighty deeds.”
Or “keep” (so KJV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
5:15 "You shall remember" See note at Deut. 7:18.

▣ "that you were a slave in the land of Egypt" Moses uses this experience of slavery to motivate the
Israelites to compassionate action toward underprivileged people in their society:

- to allow servants (and animals) a day of rest ‒ Deut. 5:12-15; 16:12

- to freely release and empower Hebrew slaves ‒ Deut. 15:12-15

- to be fair and just with the underprivileged and disenfranchised ‒ Deut. 24:17-18

- to leave the corners of the field and the second gathering of crops for the poor ‒ Deut. 24:19-22 (i.e. gleaning)

This phrase is also used numerous times to warn Israel to act appropriately in light of YHWH's
gracious gift of the land (e.g. Deut. 6:10-15) and to obey the covenant (e.g. Deut. 8:1-10) lest serious consequences come
(e.g. Deut. 8:11-20)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLEANINGS

▣ "hand" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

verses.zh: 「『当照耶和华―你　神所吩咐的孝敬父母，使你得福，并使你的日子在耶和华―你　神所赐你的地上得以长久。
verses.en: “Honor[NOTE:1] your father and your mother just as the Lord your God has commanded you to do, so that your days may be extended and that it may go well with you in the land that he[NOTE:2] is about to give you.
notes: The imperative here means, literally, “regard as heavy” (כַּבֵּד, kabbed). The meaning is that great importance must be ascribed to parents by their children.
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “He” in 5:3.
verses.commentary:
5:16 "Honor" This VERB (BDB 457, KB 455, Piel IMPERATIVE) originally
meant "to be heavy" and developed a metaphorical meaning of "give due weight to" or "honor." This honor is not based
on agreement, but authority and respect. In a sense it models the relationship between God and mankind. A submissive
attitude toward authority is crucial in religious life!

Jesus mentions these commandments several times as well as other portions of Deuteronomy:

- Deut. 5:16 ‒ Matt. 15:4; Mark 7:10

- Deut. 5:16-20 ‒ Matt. 19:18-19a; Mark 10:19; Luke 18:20

- Deut. 5:17 ‒ Matt. 5:21

- Deut. 6:4-5 ‒ Matt. 22:37; Mark 12:29-30; Luke 10:27

- Deut. 6:13 ‒ Matt. 4:10; Luke 4:8

- Deut. 6:16 ‒ Matt. 4:7; Luke 4:12

- Deut. 19:15 ‒ Matt. 18:16

- Deut. 19:15 ‒ Matt. 5:38

Paul also quotes Deuteronomy often:

- Deut. 5:16 ‒ Eph. 6:2-3

- Deut. 5:21 ‒ Rom. 7:7

- Deut. 19:15 ‒ 2 Cor. 13:1

- Deut. 21:23 ‒ Gal. 3:13

- Deut. 25:4 ‒ 2 Cor. 9:9; 1 Tim. 5:18

- Deut. 27:26 ‒ Gal. 3:10

- Deut. 30:12-14 ‒ Rom. 10:6-8

- Deut. 32:21 ‒ Rom. 11:8

- Deut. 32:35 ‒ Rom. 12:19-20

- Deut. 32:43 ‒ Rom. 15:10

(cf. Richard N. Longenecker, Biblical Exegesis in the Apostolic Period, pp. 42-43, 92-95). Apparently
the NT writers used the OT extensively, but not legalistically!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HONOR FATHER AND MOTHER

▣ "and your mother" This shows high regard for motherhood even though in the Oriental society
women were legally on the level of chattel or property. A Hebrew mother was honored in her own home. The authority
of parents was strictly respected (cf. Exod. 21:17; Deut. 27:16). Both were to be respected and obeyed
(cf. Prov. 1:8; 6:20; 15:20; 19:26; 20:20; 23:22-25; 30:11,17).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

▣ "your days may be prolonged" Verse 33; 4:40; 11:9 show that this was a promise to a society, not
primarily to an individual. If a society is characterized by honor in the home and respect for family life, that society
will be stable and last through time. See note at Deut. 4:40.

verses.zh: 「『不可杀人。
verses.en: “You must not murder.[NOTE:1]
notes: Traditionally “kill” (so KJV, ASV, RSV, NAB). The verb here (רָצַח, ratsakh) is generic for homicide but in the OT both killing in war and capital punishment were permitted and even commanded (Deut 13:5, 9; 20:13, 16-17), so the technical meaning here is “murder.”
verses.commentary:
5:17-21 These are laws that are common to all eastern societies. From archaeological discoveries we
know of the Babylonian Law Codes of Lipit-Ishtar and Hammurabi which predate the Law of Moses by several
hundred years. The Code of Hammurabi is similar to the Ten Commandments. This similarity shows

- that there are some things that are innately wrong in every situation and society

- that Moses was a child of his own day and culture as well as a prophet of God

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE

5:17 "murder" The Hebrew VERB "murder" (BDB 953, KB 1283, Qal IMPERFECT)
originally meant "to violently crush." Life belongs to God. This does not mean killing of any kind because Israel had both
capital punishment (e.g. Num. 35:30) and Holy War (e.g. 20:13,16-17). The commandment is saying "Thou shalt not violently
murder for selfish reasons or revenge" or "do not commit non-legal, premeditated murder." In my opinion this passage cannot
be used as a biblical admonition against military service or capital punishment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NOTES ON EXODUS 20 (MURDER)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE AND WAR

verses.zh: 「『不可奸淫。
verses.en: “You must not commit adultery.
verses.commentary:
5:18 "adultery" In the OT adultery (BDB 610, KB 658, Qal IMPERFECT) refers to only
extramarital sexual activities. This was a serious crime because of OT views of the afterlife. They believed that in
some sense a person lived on through his seed. Also, the importance of tribes inheriting and passing on land allotted
to them by YHWH made adultery a significant issue.

Notice, the first law is faithfulness to parents; the second law is faithfulness in not taking your
brother's life; the third idea is faithfulness within the home. Even betrothed women were treated as married (cf. Deut. 22:23ff).
Mary was accused of unfaithfulness because she was betrothed to Joseph.

This idea of adultery is often used symbolically for idolatry (i.e. spiritual adultery). Ezekiel and Hosea
analogously present YHWH as a husband to Israel, therefore, when Israel went after other gods, it was called "going a
whoring" and was considered spiritual adultery or faithlessness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ADULTERY

verses.zh: 「『不可偷盗。
verses.en: “You must not steal.
verses.commentary:
5:19 "steal" This is probably a reference to kidnaping and selling (BDB 170, KB 198, Qal IMPERFECT,
cf. Deut. 24:7; Exod. 21:16), because of the context of the surrounding laws. This expresses a faithfulness to one's covenant brother
whose life belongs to God. All of the surrounding laws brought the death penalty. This seems harsh for petty theft.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STEALING

verses.zh: 「『不可作假见证陷害人。
verses.en: “You must not offer false testimony against another.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your neighbor.” Clearly this is intended generically, however, and not to be limited only to those persons who live nearby (frequently the way “neighbor” is understood in contemporary contexts). So also in v. 20.
verses.commentary:
5:20 "bear false witness" In ancient societies, when accused of something, it was the responsibility of the
accused to prove the accuser wrong rather than our modern American judicial practice of assuming one innocent until
proven guilty. If you proved your accuser wrong he had to take the penalty for the crime he accused you of
(cf. Deut. 19:16-21). Since disobedience to the Ten Words caused death, false witness was a serious crime! Bearing
false witness reveals an unfaithfulness within the community of faith. Lies destroy the reputation and take an innocent
life of a covenant brother or sister. God takes this lying seriously (cf. Job 17:5; Ps. 101:5; Prov. 11:9; Jer. 9:8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FALSE WITNESS

verses.zh: 「『不可贪恋人的妻子；也不可贪图人的房屋、田地、仆婢、牛、驴，并他一切所有的。』
verses.en: You must not desire[NOTE:1] another man’s[NOTE:2] wife, nor should you crave his[NOTE:3] house, his field, his male and female servants, his ox, his donkey, or anything else he owns.”[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew verb used here (חָמַד, khamad) is different from the one translated “crave” (אָוַה, ʾavah) in the next line. The former has sexual overtones (“lust” or the like; cf. Song of Sol 2:3) whereas the latter has more the idea of a desire or craving for material things.
Heb “your neighbor’s.” See note on the term “fellow man” in v. 19.
Heb “your neighbor’s.” The pronoun is used in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “or anything that is your neighbor’s.”
verses.commentary:
5:21 "shall not covet. . .shall not desire" These two VERBS are synonymous:

- "covet" ‒ BDB 326, KB 325, Qal IMPERFECT, means "a strong desire" for material
things, which can be positive or negative. In this context it is an uncontrollable, selfish desire for something
which belongs to a covenant brother.

- "desire" ‒ BDB 16, KB 20, Hithpael IMPERFECT, means "desire" (cf. Deut. 14:26)
or "lust" (often has a sexual context as in Deut. 5:21) for more and more for me at any cost (e.g. Num. 11:4;
Ps. 106:14; Prov. 13:4; 21:26; 23:3,6; 24:1).

This relates to one's inner attitudes and motives. It is capstone to all the other commandments. This is
the only commandment that deals with why, not how. This one says not only "don't do" but "don't think this." Jesus taught
that we should not only not kill, we should not hate, or display an attitude that might result in murder. Jesus took this
last commandment and raised the rest of the commandments to the level of inner motive and attitude as over against
outer action (cf. Matt. 5:17-48). There is all the difference in the world in a man who does not steal because it is not
pleasing to God and the man who does not steal because he is afraid of getting caught. One is acting on biblical
principles and the other is acting on self-interest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVETING

verses.zh: 「这些话是耶和华在山上，从火中、云中、幽暗中，大声晓谕你们全会众的；此外并没有添别的话。他就把这话写在两块石版上，交给我了。」
verses.en: The Lord said these things to your entire assembly at the mountain from the middle of the fire, the cloud, and the darkness with a loud voice, and that was all he said.[NOTE:1] Then he inscribed the words[NOTE:2] on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
notes: Heb “and he added no more” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV); NLT “This was all he said at that time.”
Heb “them”; the referent (the words spoken by the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
5:22 "He added no more" The Ten Words (Decalog) and their explanations are from YHWH, not Moses
(compare Exod. 31:18 & 34:27-28). This is revelation (from God), not human discovery or rationalization. The
phrase "and He added no more" is a literary way of asserting a complete revelation (cf. Deut. 4:2; 12:32).

Verses 22-27 are referring to the experience of Israel at Mt. Horeb/Sinai and recorded in Exodus 19-20.

This revelation must be respected and untampered with (cf. Deut. 4:2; 12:32; Prov. 30:6; Eccl. 3:14).

verses.zh: 「那时，火焰烧山，你们听见从黑暗中出来的声音；你们支派中所有的首领和长老都来就近我，
verses.en: Then, when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness while the mountain was ablaze, all your tribal leaders and elders approached me.
verses.commentary:
5:23 "all the heads of your tribes and your elders" The elders came to Moses because they were frightened
(cf. Deut. 5:25-26; Exod. 19:16,18; 20:18-20) by the physical manifestations connected to YHWH's personal presence
on Mt. Horeb/Sinai.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

SPECIAL TOPIC: CAN HUMANS SEE GOD AND LIVE?

verses.zh: 说：『看哪，耶和华―我们　神将他的荣光和他的大能显给我们看，我们又听见他的声音从火中出来。今日我们得见　神与人说话，人还存活。
verses.en: You said, “The Lord our God has shown us his great glory,[NOTE:1] and we have heard him speak from the middle of the fire. It is now clear to us[NOTE:2] that God can speak to human beings and they can keep on living.
notes: Heb “his glory and his greatness.”
Heb “this day we have seen.”
verses.commentary:
5:24 "His glory and His greatness" The Hebrew root "glory" (BDB 458; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY [OT]) is the same
root as "honor" (BDB 457) of Deut. 5:16. Both are commercial terms meaning "heavy" or "weighty," which came to denote
honor. It is used often of God's

- name (e.g. Ps. 29:2; 66:2; 79:9; 96:8)

- person (e.g. Exod. 24:16-17; 33:18,22; 40:34-35; Num. 14:22)

- actions (e.g. Exod. 16:7,12)

The second term "greatness" (BDB 152) is often used of God in Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 3:24; 5:24;
9:26; 11:2; 32:3; Ps. 150:2). See notes at Deut. 4:31 and 10:17.

▣ "that God speaks with man" God does reveal Himself and humanity can understand and relate to
Him! This is the basis of our understanding of God's revelation and God's covenant requirements.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

verses.zh: 现在这大火将要烧灭我们，我们何必冒死呢？若再听见耶和华―我们　神的声音就必死亡。
verses.en: But now, why should we die, because this intense fire will consume us? If we keep hearing the voice of the Lord our God we will die!

verses.zh: 凡属血气的，曾有何人听见永生　神的声音从火中出来，像我们听见还能存活呢？
verses.en: Who is there from the entire human race[NOTE:1] who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire as we have, and has lived?
notes: Heb “who is there of all flesh.”

verses.zh: 求你近前去，听耶和华―我们　神所要说的一切话，将他对你说的话都传给我们，我们就听从遵行。』
verses.en: You go near so that you can hear everything the Lord our God is saying and then you can tell us whatever he[NOTE:1] says to you; then we will pay attention and do it.”
notes: Heb “the Lord our God.” See note on “He” in 5:3.
verses.commentary:
5:27 "Go near and hear all that the Lord our God says" This has two Qal
IMPERATIVE VERBS:

- "go near" ‒ BDB 897, KB 1132, which means "come near" or "approach." Approaching YHWH often had
dangerous consequences (cf. Exod. 16:7; Lev. 16:1; Num. 16:16).

- "hear" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, this is the often repeated VERB shema (i.e. "we will hear and do it")

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

verses.zh: 「你们对我说的话，耶和华都听见了。耶和华对我说：『这百姓的话，我听见了；他们所说的都是。
verses.en: When the Lord heard you speaking to me, he[NOTE:1] said to me, “I have heard what these people have said to you—they have spoken well.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “He” in 5:3.
verses.commentary:
5:28-33 Notice that God says "that it may be well for you." These commandments weren't given to burden
the people. God gave them to give His people freedom. God gave His laws to give us a whole, healthy, and happy life.
They are necessary because of the fall of humanity in Adam.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

verses.zh: 惟愿他们存这样的心敬畏我，常遵守我的一切诫命，使他们和他们的子孙永远得福。
verses.en: If only it would really be their desire to fear me and obey[NOTE:1] all my commandments in the future, so that it may go well with them and their descendants forever.
notes: Heb “keep” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
5:29 "Oh that they had such a heart. . .and would keep all My commandments" This introductory exclamation
("Oh that they had," BDB 566 plus BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERFECT) is a common phrase in the
OT used twenty-five times, mostly in Job (NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 209). Here it expresses a wish (cf. 2 Sam. 18:33; Ps. 55:6).

God longs for mankind's happiness and peace, but this involves responsibilities. If they would obey, it
would be good for them, for their children, for their children's children and on and on (cf. Deut. 27-29).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

verses.zh: 你去对他们说：你们回帐棚去吧！
verses.en: Go and tell them, ‘Return to your tents!’
verses.commentary:
5:30,31 These two verses have a series of commands:

- "go" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:30

- "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:30

- "return" ‒ BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:30

- "stand" ‒ BDB 763, KB 840, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:31

- "speak" ‒ BDB 180, KB 210, Qal IMPERATIVE, Deut. 5:31

- "teach" ‒ BDB 540, KB 531, Piel IMPERFECT (possibly in this context
COHORTATIVE in meaning), Deut. 5:31

verses.zh: 至于你，可以站在我这里，我要将一切诫命、律例、典章传给你；你要教训他们，使他们在我赐他们为业的地上遵行。』
verses.en: But as for you, remain here with me so I can declare to you all the commandments,[NOTE:1] statutes, and ordinances that you are to teach them, so that they can carry them out in the land I am about to give them.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “commandment.” The MT actually has the singular (הַמִּצְוָה, hammitsvah), suggesting perhaps that the following terms (חֻקִּים [khuqqim] and מִשְׁפָּטִים [mishpatim]) are in epexegetical apposition to “commandment.” That is, the phrase could be translated “the entire command, namely, the statutes and ordinances.” This would essentially make מִצְוָה (mitsvah) synonymous with תּוֹרָה (torah), the usual term for the whole collection of law.
Heb “to possess it” (so KJV, ASV); NLT “as their inheritance.”
verses.commentary:
5:31 "all the commandments and the statutes and the judgments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

▣ "which I give them to possess" There are two VERBALS in this phrase:

- "give" ‒ BDB, 678, KB 733, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE

- "to possess" ‒ BDB, 429, KB 441, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

This statement is based on:

- God's promise to Abraham, Gen. 12:1-3; 15:18-21

- God's promise to Isaac, Gen. 26:3-5

- God's promise to Jacob, Gen. 28:13-15; 35:9-12

- God's promise to Israel, Gen. 15:16; Exod. 6:4,8; Deut. 4:38,40; 19:10; 20:16; 21:23;
Josh. 1:2,3,6,11,13,15; 2:9,24; 18:3; 21:43; 24:13

God gave/promised a special land to Israel, but Israel had to

- take it

- settle it

- maintain covenant faithfulness in it (i.e. conditional covenant, cf. Deut. 4:40; 7:12-13; 8:1-20)

verses.zh: 所以，你们要照耶和华―你们　神所吩咐的谨守遵行，不可偏离左右。
verses.en: Be careful, therefore, to do exactly what the Lord your God has commanded you; do not turn right or left!
verses.commentary:
5:32 "you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left" This is an idiom related to God's word as a clearly
defined path or road (cf. Ps. 119:105; Prov. 6:23). To deviate from God's clear path/road was sin (cf. Deut. 9:12,16;
17:11,20; 28:14; Josh. 1:7; 23:6; 31:29; 2 Kgs. 22:2; 2 Chr. 34:2; Prov. 4:27). See note at Deut. 2:27.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WAY. . .THE PATH

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们　神所吩咐你们行的，你们都要去行，使你们可以存活得福，并使你们的日子在所要承受的地上得以长久。」
verses.en: Walk just as he[NOTE:1] has commanded you so that you may live, that it may go well with you, and that you may live long[NOTE:2] in the land you are going to possess.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “may prolong your days”; NAB “may have long life”; TEV “will continue to live.”
verses.commentary:
5:33 "You shall walk" In this context "walk" means "lifestyle" (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERFECT).
Biblical faith is not only laws to be kept, it is a daily lifestyle: 24 hours a day, 7 days-a-week relationship to YHWH by faith. This
faith must issues in a godly life (i.e. Eph. 2:10; 4:1,17; 5:2,15). Obedience is the evidence of this faith relationship, not the basis or mechanism.

▣ "that it may be well with" The VERB (BDB 373, KB 370, Qal PERFECT
with waw) is literally "pleasing" or "good." The ADJECTIVE is often used to describe the Promised Land
(cf. Deut. 1:25,25; 3:25; 4:21,22, etc.). The VERB describes the good life God promises for covenant
obedience (cf. Deut. 15:16; 19:13).

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 1, pp. 143-144, lists the OT law codes:

- the Decalogue ‒ Exod. 20:2-17; Deut. 5:6-21

- the Code of the Covenant ‒ Exod. 20:22-23:33

- Deuteronomy ‒ Deuteronomy 12-26

- the Law of Holiness ‒ Leviticus 17-26

- the Priestly code ‒ Leviticus 11-16 (BDB 435)

All of these are considered Torah (BDB 435). They are specific divine prescriptions on actions and attitudes.

- Types of Israeli laws

- Casuistic ‒ laws characterized by the "if. . .then" format. There are consequences to actions. These
are usually guidelines for societies.

- Apodictic ‒ laws stated as general prohibitions (usually SECOND PERSON PLURAL
statements ‒ "you shall not. . ."). These are usually guidelines for the spiritual life.
SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE

- Cultural influences

- in content ‒ earlier law codes

- Lipit-Ishtar

- Code of Hammurabi

- in form ‒ Hittite treaties (Suzerain), which occur in several set patterns, but Deuteronomy and
Joshua 24 follow the pattern of the 2000 B.C. period, which shows
its historicity (cf. John H. Walton, Ancient Israelite Literature in Its Cultural Context, pp. 95-107;
K. A. Kitchen, The Bible in Its World, pp. 80-95; see introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

- The words of Exodus 20 have been slightly changed. These ten words were said to have been written by the
finger of God. Therefore, which version, Exod. 20 or Deut. 20:5, is original?

I think Moses modified lthe Exod. 20 version given to a nomadic desert community for a people about to
enter and settle down in Canaan. For a good brief discussion, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 172-173.
